<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` commands will fetch the source archive from the official GitHub repository (https://github.com/Vencord/builds) at a specific commit SHA, which is a legitimate and expected source. The PKGBUILD defines standard package functions for multiple Vencord variants (vencord-bin, chromium-vencord-bin, firefox-vencord-bin, etc.) and uses proper package() functions to install files to appropriate system directories. During source fetching and PKGBUILD parsing, no code is executed - only the source array is evaluated (which references a URL) and the package functions are defined. The sha256sums are present and valid. There are no top-level commands, no pkgver() function that executes code, and no suspicious network operations in the global scope. All source definitions point to the official Vencord GitHub repository at a pinned commit, which is expected behavior for a package distribution.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>

- No network requests or downloads
- No file operations, system modifications, or privilege escalation
- No obfuscation, encoding, or use of dangerous commands (eval, base64, curl, etc.)
- No data exfiltration or external communication

The mention of disabling `xpinstall.signatures.required` for Zen is merely textual advice printed to the user — the script does not modify any configuration files itself. This is consistent with the upstream requirement for installing unsigned XPI extensions in Firefox-based browsers.

The file represents entirely normal post-install messaging for a packaging helper script.
